subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit; its footage supplies the camera, framing, background, lighting, set objects, and it contains the single person on screen who is being replaced.
<Subject 1> is the replacement person. Their identity, facial features, hairstyle, skin, body build and outfit come from the person in the reference photograph <Picture 1>; their position in the frame, scale, body proportion, pose, timing and movement come from the one person in <Video 1> whom they replace. They are the only element of the footage that is changed. The photograph <Picture 1> is an appearance source only and is never itself shown: neither the photograph, nor its backdrop, nor the studio lighting it was shot under appears anywhere in the target video.
<Subject 2> is the preserved production of <Video 1>: the camera angle and any camera movement, framing and composition, depth of field, background and every object in the set, lighting direction and quality, color grade, and image texture, all carried over unchanged. <Video 1> contains exactly one person and no other human figure appears at any point in it.
<Audio 1> is the synchronized audio track of <Video 1> and is reused in the target video.

summary:
[video editing + audio reuse] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The single person on screen in <Video 1> is replaced by <Subject 1>, whose identity, hairstyle, skin, build and outfit come from the person in the reference photograph <Picture 1> and whose position, scale, pose, timing and movement are inherited from the person they replace. Nothing else in the footage is altered: the frame still contains exactly one person before and after the edit, and the reference photograph and its own background never appear on screen.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout the target video): attribute_transfer - the identity, facial features, hairstyle, skin, body build and outfit of the person in <Picture 1> are transferred onto the position, scale, body proportion, pose, timing and movement taken from the single person in <Video 1>.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout the target video): fully_preserved - the camera angle and movement, framing, depth of field, background and its objects, lighting, color grade and image texture are retained exactly as in <Video 1>, and the footage continues to contain one person and no more.
<Video 1> (edit source, full duration): partially_preserved - the source footage is edited only in the one person on screen; all of its remaining content is carried over unchanged.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - the original synchronized audio track of <Video 1> is reused 1:1 as the target video's audio.

detailed_description:
The target video is an edited version of <Video 1> and keeps the source footage's photographic rendering, aspect ratio, resolution, grain and color grade; the single change to the footage is the replacement of one person, and nothing else about how the video looks, is lit or moves is altered.
[Shot 1] The edit runs across the entire clip and does not add, remove, reorder or retime any shot; if <Video 1> contains cuts, the target video cuts at exactly the same frames. From the very first frame, the sole person visible in <Video 1> is replaced by <Subject 1>, whose identity, facial features, hairstyle, skin, body build and outfit are taken from the person in the reference photograph <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> holds exactly the same position in the frame, at exactly the same scale and body proportion, in exactly the same pose, and follows exactly the same movement — the same timing, the same trajectory, the same gestures and the same screen direction — as the person they replace, continuously from the opening frame to the final one. Their appearance is regenerated only within the silhouette and screen area that the replaced person occupied, so the frame still holds one person, standing or moving where that person stood and moved. They stay fully consistent in face, hair and clothing as the shot progresses, including when the camera changes angle, distance or exposure.
They are lit only by the light that already exists in <Video 1>: the reference photograph's own backdrop, background color and studio lighting are not transferred, and they take on <Subject 2>'s lighting direction, contrast and color grade so that they sit naturally inside the source footage's scene.
Every remaining element of <Subject 2> is carried over from <Video 1> untouched and unmoved: the camera angle and any camera movement, the framing and composition, the depth of field, the background and the entire set of objects within it, the lighting direction and quality, the color grade and the image texture. No additional person, prop, effect, set element, logo or overlay is introduced anywhere in the frame, and nothing present in the source footage is removed or obscured.
The reference photograph <Picture 1> is never displayed. It does not appear as a picture, thumbnail, inset, frame or reflection anywhere at any time, and its own background, backdrop or studio setting never enters the target video's scene.

overall_soundscape:
<Audio 1>, the original ambience, physical sounds and any audible voices of <Video 1>, continues unchanged throughout the target video; the replacement introduces no new sound and removes none.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A - any audience-only score already present in <Video 1> is carried over as part of <Audio 1>.
